To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

persistence of fecal indicator bacteria in subtropical freshwater and saltwater environments is influenced by water type, sediment, and inoculum type, and that persistence of E. coli strains is influenced by strain.

fecal coliform and enterococcal persistence in freshwater was significantly different from that in saltwater, persistence in sediments was different from that in the water column, and persistence of E. coli strains was variable.
persistence of indicator bacteria is dependent on water type, sediment location, E. coli strain, and inoculum type.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fate and persistence of fecal bacteria, including fecal indicators, in water and sediment environments.
the persistence and differential survival of fecal indicator bacteria in environmental waters.
the persistence and differential survival of fecal indicator bacteria in subtropical water and sediments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fecal coliform and enterococcus decay rates are influenced by water type, IO, inoculum source, and location within the mesocosm.
fecal pollution in the water environment is a function of the persistence of fecal coliforms and/or enterococci and the relative abundance of these bacteria.

persistence of fecal coliforms and fecal enterococci is influenced by a variety of factors including the source of the feces, the type of water, the type of sediment, and the type of indicator organism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fecal indicator persistence in water is dependent on the IO, the inoculum, the environment, and the strain.
persistence of indicator bacteria is highly variable, depending on water type, sediment or water column location, inoculum, and IO.
fecal pollution is a complex phenomenon that is influenced by many factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fecal indicator bacteria do not persist equally in environmental water, and that persistence varies according to the source of contamination.
fecal coliforms and Enterococcus faecalis persist longer in freshwater environments than in saltwater.
the use of a single indicator to monitor water quality is problematic because of differences in persistence among strains.
